name: Pterodactylus
isnote: Recovered as the most basal member of Euctenochasmatia.
sum: The first pterosaur ever named, from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria.
wsnote: About 1.04 m, based on the only known adult.
holotype: BSP AS.I.739 — Solnhofen limestone, Eichstätt, Bavaria (described 1784).
material: Over 30 specimens, mostly juveniles, many complete.
exceptional: Some specimens show a low bony crest and an occipital lappet.
biology: A generalist carnivore; tooth wear suggests it mainly ate invertebrates.
author: Cuvier 1809
